videos.script: How reliable should the shop be? Every answer people give first is wrong. Always up is impossible, and as reliable as possible has no number in it. {{question}} This lesson puts a number on it, in three steps. First, a measurement of what customers get: the share of checkouts that did not fail. That is the indicator. {{sli}} Then a target for that measurement over a window. Ninety-nine and a half per cent. That is the objective. {{slo}} And then the part that changes how a team works. The half per cent that may fail is a budget, and it can be spent. {{budget}} The lab spends some of it. For four minutes, one charge in twenty fails, and you watch an hour's budget drain. {{incident}} The last question is what a team does when the budget runs out. That has to be agreed before it happens. {{policy}}
